description: Challenge A2 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Plaid has the /æ/ vowel. Played has /eɪ/, plead has /i/, and plied has /aɪ/.
Swept has the short /ɛ/ vowel and ends with /t/. Swapped has /æ/, while sweeped and swapt are not standard spellings.
Rough has /ʌ/ in General American. Roof has /u/ or /ʊ/ depending on speaker, rouge has /uːʒ/, and row has /oʊ/.
Genre begins with /ʒ/, as in the middle sound of measure. The other words begin with /dʒ/.
Choir begins with /kw/ in General American. Quire has the same pronunciation but is a different, uncommon word; wire and fire begin with /w/ and /f/.
Thief begins with /θ/. Chief begins with /tʃ/, sheaf with /ʃ/, and leaf with /l/.
Breath ends with unvoiced /θ/. Bread ends with /d/, breed with /d/, and breathe ends with voiced /ð/.
Clothes is commonly pronounced with final /ðz/ in General American. Close ends in /z/, clothe in /ð/, and clocks in /ks/.
Asked ends with /t/ after the /s/ sound. Ask has no final /t/, asks ends with /s/, and acting ends with /ŋ/.
Enough uses gh to spell the final /f/ sound. The other spellings are not standard English.
Island has a silent s; the word begins with the vowel sound /aɪ/. The other forms are not standard spellings.
Receipt uses ei after c to spell the /i/ sound, and p is silent. The other options misspell the word.
